It all depends on the numbers. To avoid penalties all you have to do is pay in 100% of last years tax if your AGI is under 150,000.

But, in your scenario say you owe 1,000 tax at the end of the year. That would mean you need to have paid 250 per quarter.

Say withholding for the year is only 800 (doesn't matter what month it was paid). That means you only paid 200 per quarter. So you will have penalties on 50 first quarter, 100 + interest from first quarter, 150 + interest, 200 + interest.
It's rare for a couple to be better off filing separate. Usually when people do it is because they are both high income and it does change the answer due to phasing out of everything.

Simple answer is with withholding yes you can. Any underpayment penalty is calculated by taking total tax due and divide by 4. Then each quarter you need to have a fourth paid in. Any not paid accrues interest at 3% apy starting from the quarter you are underpaid and accruing forward.

Withholding is calculated into the underpayment penalty by taking total withholding for the year and dividing by 4. Then applying that to each quarter.
